cause.fact: The std::less<llvm::rdf::RegisterRef> specialization contains a PhysicalRegisterInfo pointer and calls PRI->less(A,B). It is stateful and not default-constructible.
RegisterRef deliberately deletes operator<, operator== and operator!=; target-aware ordering cannot be replaced by the raw operators.
In C++14 and later, the SDK's __make_transparent<T,less<T>> unconditionally selects less<void>; there is no predicate testing whether a user specialization retained the original semantics.
std::set insertion enters __emplace_unique, then __find_equal, then __as_transparent<Key>(value_comp()). The conversion path is selected even though the comparator instance carries PRI state.

When the comparator type changes, __as_transparent asserts is_empty<Comparator>, ignores the original instance, and default-constructs the transparent comparator. The PRI pointer makes the assertion fail.
The substituted less<void> calls operator<; RegisterRef's deleted operator produces the two further comparison errors. Removing only the static_assert would not restore PRI-dependent semantics.
